Address.description:
A position in a language's namespace: the package it belongs to and the
path within it — `fff :: [grep, types]` for a Rust module, path
components for a TypeScript file. Prefix relations, which are what a move
cares about, never hold across packages.

Diff.description:
One file's change: the unified diff text (the wire) and its hunks (the
model).

FileChange.description: One file a plan touches: its edits and the whole-file diff.

moved_to.description: Path after, when the file is moved.

MoveIntent.description: Move a file and make every reference to it follow.

Name.description: One identifier: a module, a declaration, a file stem. Compared by text.

Notice.description:
Something a plan could not do and a human should look at. Never fatal:
the rest of the plan is still valid. Data only; the display layer words it.

oneOf.description:
An import the layout understood but the surgery could not rewrite in place;
`replacement` is what it should become.

After the move, `from` references `item` but may not see it, and the
widening it would take is not one vvv makes on its own (making a
declaration public across packages is the author's call).

An import that now names a declaration in its own file, inside a
grouped statement vvv does not split for this; remove the entry.

PackageId.description:
The name a package goes by in paths: a Rust crate's lib name (`fff`, not
`fff-search`), a TypeScript package's name. The layout decides the spelling.

Position.description:
Zero-based line and character column. Columns count `char`s, not bytes,
so they are safe to show to humans and editors.

ReachKind.description: What a visibility modifier means, relative to the declaring module.

oneOf.description: The declaring module and its descendants (Rust private).
The parent module and its descendants (`pub(super)`).
A module named in the modifier (`pub(in a::b)`); the layout resolves it.

RelPath.description:
A file's path inside the workspace, spelled the way the project does: `/`
on every platform.

A workspace path is a project path — like a `mod` path or a
`crate::a::b` address — not a path of the machine, so it carries its own
spelling and is what goes on the wire, into a row, or into a diagnostic.
It reads as a [`Path`] (an OS path is made from one at the edge, where a
file is actually read), but it cannot spell a separator the host's way:
`Display`, serde and the stored bytes are always `/`.

Respelling.description:
A reference a move re-spelled in place: where it is, what it said and
what it says now. A preview lists these as one row each instead of a
diff hunk; an edit no respelling accounts for is structural and shows as
a hunk.

span.description: The reference's span before the move — the edit that rewrites it.

Span.description: Half-open byte range `[start, end)` inside a single file.

description: `vvv move`: a file or directory moved, its importers respelled.

from_address.description: The module address before and after, when the language has one.

notices.description: References vvv found but could not rewrite.

respellings.description:
References rewritten in place; every other edit in `files` is
structural (a `mod` line moved, a visibility widened).
